note: Example fleet layout. Copy to fleet.json (gitignored) or point LEH_FLEET_CONFIG at your copy. Hosts are ssh names (one user, same home on every host); runner names must look like wave<digits>. accounts maps an account label to a secret reference: runners need file: references to a token file that you place on each host yourself (mode 600); deploy only checks it.

host-1.note: A slower host: fewer active runners, more free memory required.

policy_note: Up to max_rounds rounds while the frontier moves; one ROUTE_REVIEW lineage before a stalled lineage ends; retries from the best finished files with no size cap (retry_max_ref_modules 0), at most max_retries; problems whose size hint ref_min_modules is at least program_min_ref_modules and that stall after a route review become lane programs.
policy_note_20261014: docs/FEEDER-POLICY.md: verification_seconds 21600 (the evaluation CI allows 6 h); a complete but unverified round gets a 1-round VERIFY lineage (verify_lineages; then CI_FIT on a timeout, REPAIR on a rejection; at most max_verifies per problem); residual progress needs a proved row or a lower estimate; stall when the estimate falls by less than 25% (estimate_stall_ratio) twice, else after churn_rounds rounds without a new sorry minimum; quota_handoff moves paused lineages to an idle runner with quota as RESUME; max_active_runners, min_mem_available_gb and max_memory_pressure_avg60 close assignment on a loaded host (0 or null = off). leaderboard_model: the model id under which the public leaderboard credits your submissions (its problems are skipped), null = no filter. contributors: tags written into packages, e.g. ["@your-handle"].

publish.note: Operator machine only (local/publish.py, local/verify_current.py): the private repository that receives one claude/<problem>-private branch per solved problem, the organizers' intake repository and the account whose results file there lists credited problems (null = no skip).

coordinator.note: local/coordinator.py (operator machine), docs/COORDINATOR-POLICY.md. hosts: relative single-lineage throughput and whether heavy (hard/extreme tier) single lineages may run there.
